ground.reason: WIK-A1 checks specified ages in one fixture. It does not discharge "An archiving run archives every stale page" for the remaining ages and run contexts.

objections.objection: Pages outside the tested age cases can remain unarchived despite being stale.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the 400-day page remains searchable and has no archived banner.
scenario.given: An implementation handles every criterion's fixtures correctly but skips pages last edited exactly 400 days ago.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, and an archiving run encounters a 400-day page.

ground.reason: WIK-A1 checks one viewing history. D1's statement "Viewing a page is not an edit" applies beyond that history.

objections.objection: Viewing can change archiving eligibility in cases other than the tested recently viewed 366-day page.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the viewed page's last-edit time advances and it escapes archiving.
scenario.given: Viewing resets the last-edit time for pages with six revisions; the criterion fixtures do not exercise that viewing case.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then someone views a stale six-revision page before an archiving run.

ground.reason: The checks use a title query and one content-phrase query. D2 promises that an archived page "appears in no search result," which includes other queries.

objections.objection: An archived page can be excluded from the tested searches while appearing in another search result.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but a query using a different matching phrase returns the archived page.
scenario.given: Search excludes archived pages for the exact queries used by the tests but includes them for other matching queries.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then a reader searches for a different phrase from an archived page's content.

ground.reason: URL checks cover the archived pages exercised by WIK-A1 and WIK-A3. D2 says an archived page's URL "returns HTTP 200" with the specified banner above its content without limiting this to those pages.

objections.objection: Other archived pages can fail the URL and banner contract.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the existing archived page's URL returns HTTP 404.
scenario.given: Pages archived in the criterion fixtures serve correctly, while a page archived before those fixtures returns HTTP 404.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then a reader opens the existing archived page's URL.

ground.reason: The criteria check selected unarchived pages and queries. D2 promises that a page that is not archived "appears in search for its title and its content, and its URL shows no banner" generally.

objections.objection: Unarchived pages outside the checked cases can lose search visibility or display an archived banner.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the unarchived page displays the archived banner.
scenario.given: The implementation renders the checked unarchived pages correctly but displays an archived banner on another unarchived page.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then a reader opens that unarchived page.

ground.reason: WIK-A3 exercises one restoration case. D3 promises "Pressing Restore on an archived page makes it not archived" without restricting the page's revision count or history.

objections.objection: Restore can fail for archived pages outside the exercised restoration case.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the page remains archived after Restore is pressed.
scenario.given: Restore works for WIK-A3's page but does nothing for an archived page with six revisions.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then an editor presses Restore on the six-revision page.

ground.reason: WIK-A3 checks eligibility exactly 365 days and 365 days plus one second after restoration. D3 says restoration "counts as an edit of the page at that moment for D1," committing to eligibility throughout the resulting time interval.

objections.objection: The two tested restore boundaries can pass while eligibility at other elapsed times is wrong.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the restored page remains unarchived 366 days after restoration.
scenario.given: Restored pages become eligible for archiving only at exactly 365 days plus one second, satisfying WIK-A3's checks.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then a restored page receives its next archiving run 366 days after restoration.

ground.reason: WIK-A2 compares preservation for pages with one and five revisions. D4 promises "Archiving a page leaves its URL, its content and its revision list unchanged" for every page.

objections.objection: Initial archiving can alter a page's URL, content or revision list outside the preservation fixtures.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the six-revision page loses its oldest revision.
scenario.given: Archiving preserves pages with one and five revisions but truncates the revision list of pages with six revisions.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then an archiving run archives a stale six-revision page.

ground.reason: WIK-A2 checks an immediate second run. D4 promises that "a later archiving run over a page already archived leaves its content and its revision list unchanged," including delayed and subsequent runs.

objections.objection: Preservation can fail on a later run even though an immediate repeat preserves the page.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the delayed run removes a revision from the already archived page.
scenario.given: Immediate repeat runs preserve archived pages, but runs at least one day later truncate their revision lists.
scenario.when: All criterion checks pass in CI, then an already archived page is processed again one day later.

obligations.statement: An archiving run archives every stale page using the strict last-edit cutoff of more than 365 days; initially unarchived pages at or below the cutoff remain unarchived.
obligations.source: What changes: "An archiving run archives every stale page." D1: "A page is stale when its last edit is more than 365 days before the archiving run." The restriction to archiving stale pages plainly implies preserving initially unarchived nonstale pages.

parts.statement: The seven ages in WIK-A1 receive the checked archived or unarchived search and URL outcomes on the initial run and the immediate second run.
The cutoff produces the required archive selection for other ages, page populations and run contexts.

obligations.statement: Viewing a page does not count as an edit or change its eligibility under D1.
obligations.source: D1: "Viewing a page is not an edit, so a page viewed recently but not edited is still stale."

parts.statement: Viewing WIK-A1's 366-day page one day before the run does not prevent its checked archived outcomes.
Viewing preserves D1 eligibility for other page ages, histories and viewing patterns.

obligations.statement: Every archived page is excluded from every search result, including queries matching its title or content.
obligations.source: What changes: "An archived page drops out of search." D2: "An archived page appears in no search result, whether the query matches its title or its content."

parts.statement: Archived pages checked by WIK-A1 and WIK-A3 are absent from the specified title and content-phrase searches at the checked points.
Archived pages are absent from all remaining queries and search contexts, including searches involving other archived pages.

obligations.statement: Every archived page remains readable at its URL, returning HTTP 200 with the exact archived banner above its content.
obligations.source: What changes: "An archived page ... stays readable at its URL under a banner." D2: "its URL returns HTTP 200 with the banner \"This page is archived and may be out of date.\" above its content."

parts.statement: Archived URL opens exercised by WIK-A1 and WIK-A3 return HTTP 200 and show the specified banner above the content.
Other archived pages and URL-opening contexts satisfy the same HTTP, readability and banner requirements.

obligations.statement: Every unarchived page appears in searches for its title and content, and its URL displays no archived banner.
obligations.source: D2: "A page that is not archived appears in search for its title and its content, and its URL shows no banner."

parts.statement: Unarchived states checked by WIK-A1 and WIK-A3 have the required results for the specified title and content-phrase searches and display no banner on the checked URL opens.
Other unarchived pages, matching searches and URL-opening contexts satisfy the same search visibility and absence-of-banner requirements.

obligations.statement: An editor can make an archived page unarchived by pressing its Restore button.
obligations.source: What changes: "An editor restores an archived page with its Restore button." D3: "Pressing Restore on an archived page makes it not archived."

parts.statement: Pressing Restore in WIK-A3's restoration case produces the checked unarchived search and URL outcomes.
Restore produces the required unarchived behavior for other archived pages and restoration contexts.

obligations.statement: Restoration counts as an edit at the restoration moment for subsequent D1 eligibility.
obligations.source: D3: "the restore counts as an edit of the page at that moment for D1." D1: "A page is stale when its last edit is more than 365 days before the archiving run."

parts.statement: WIK-A3's restored page has the checked unarchived outcomes at exactly 365 days and the checked archived outcomes at 365 days plus one second after restoration.
The restoration moment determines D1 eligibility at all other elapsed times and in other restoration and subsequent-edit histories.

obligations.statement: Initial archiving preserves the page's URL, content and revision list.
obligations.source: D4: "Archiving a page leaves its URL, its content and its revision list unchanged."

parts.statement: Initial archiving of WIK-A2's 366-day pages with one and five revisions preserves their URLs and their content and revision lists as read through the page API.
Initial archiving preserves URLs, content and revision lists for other pages and archiving contexts.

obligations.statement: A later archiving run over an already archived page preserves its content and revision list.
obligations.source: D4: "a later archiving run over a page already archived leaves its content and its revision list unchanged."

parts.statement: The immediate second run over WIK-A2's two archived pages preserves their content and revision lists as read through the page API.
Delayed runs, further repetitions and runs over other already archived pages preserve their content and revision lists.

rejected.objection: Pages outside the tested age cases can remain unarchived despite being stale.
rejected.reason: WIK-A1 runs one archiving run, then a second, over a seven-page wiki, checking each page by a title search, a search for one content phrase and an open of its URL. The objection's scenario is a variant of that case, another population member: a page last edited 400 days before the run, whose specified outcome under D1 and D2 is the same, archived. The criteria fix the cases the check runs, so the objection is a variant and is rejected.
